newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav PM sees Greece trip boosting cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav PM sees Greece trip boosting cooperation.

text.p: Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic expects his forthcoming visit to Greece to boost bilateral economic cooperation and push the volume of trade between the countries to $500 million in 1998, Tanjug newsagency reported on Tuesday.
Kontic leaves for a one-day working visit to Athens on Wednesday at the invitation of his Greek counterpart, Costas Simitis.

"The talks would focus on boosting bilateral economic cooperation, Yugoslavia's full reintegration into the international community and further development of regional and multilateral cooperation in the Balkans," the agency quoted Kontic as saying.
Yugoslavia and Greece will sign two accords to facilitate economic cooperation -- one of them to protect investments and the second on avoiding double taxation, Kontic said.
He said Yugoslavia would urge liberalisation in movement of people, capital and goods between the two countries with a final aim of setting up a free-trade zone.
Such a zone might eventually all the Balkan countries, Kontic said.
Financial and banking cooperation will also be discussed.
"We will propose the opening of a mixed Yugoslav-Greek bank," he said.
"I hope we will finally agree on a $100 million commodity credit by Greece which would boost commodity trade between the two countries," he added.
Bilateral economic cooperation increased considerably since lifting of war-related sanctions last year and reached some $250 million in 1996, half the amount of the pre-sanctions level.

Kontic said the government would ask for political backing from Greece for commercial arrangements made earlier between Yugoslav businessmen and the Greek port of Salonika regarding transit of Yugoslav ships in the port.
"If all these measures are agreed on, I may safely say the volume of trade next year will amount to $500 million."
The prime minster praised Greece for its efforts to assist Yugoslavia in reintegrating itself in international political, financial and trade organisations.
"We expect Greece to urge Yugoslavia's inclusion in pan-European transport corridors at the third European conference on transportation to be held in Helsinki soon," Kontic said.

Yugoslavia was interested in particular in the new Corridor 10 and the extention of Corridor 6 which goes from Budapest via Belgrade south to the Adriatic port of Bar, with one fork leading toward Tirana in Albania.
"Yugoslavia percieves Balkan regional and multilateral integration as a way to overcome legacies of the past but also as an efficient way for joining European integration," he said.
Kontic said Yugoslavia supported Greece's proposal for Balkan summit.
